value: ABR threshold about 75 dB at 0.25 kHz (average, 4 animals); gerbil about 40 dB at the same frequency
eye: ear; ABR (summed brainstem response), not a behavioural audiogram
method: auditory brainstem response threshold, visual detection of any wave in the averaged trace
conditions: Auditory brainstem response (ABR) in anaesthetized animals (subcutaneous ketamine 35 to 50 mg/kg plus xylazine 8 mg/kg), four naked mole-rats (two breeding adults, two non-breeding adult females, 1 to 6.3 years) and two Mongolian gerbils (2 to 8 months, sex not reported); body temperature held at 30 C for the mole-rats (about their tunnel temperature) and 37 C for the gerbils, room temperature not reported. Free-field tone bursts (5 ms) at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 10 kHz from a speaker 30 cm away, level raised in 5 dB steps over a 40 dB range; the maximum level is not stated as one value (examples shown span 70 to 110 and 30 to 70). Threshold was the lowest level at which a response could be detected visually on the trace, regardless of wave, or 2.5 dB below the lowest level that elicited a measurable response. Sound level meter set to A-weighting. Nothing was tested below 0.25 kHz or above 10 kHz.

note: Printed and accepted name Heterocephalus glaber (Mammal Diversity Database taxon page 1001280: Ruppell 1842, Heterocephalidae, Rodentia). The authors note that ABR-derived curves are elevated by about 15 to 25 dB relative to behavioural audiograms for both species, so these are ABR thresholds, not behavioural ones, and they consider the mole-rat ABR audiogram consistent with the earlier behavioural audiogram. The text gives no numerical best frequency and does not report values at 8 and 10 kHz; besides the 0.25 kHz averages it gives example 2 kHz thresholds (gerbil 22.5 dB, naked mole-rat 52.5 dB), and the full curves are in Fig. 3. Both audiograms are U-shaped. n is 4 mole-rats and 2 gerbils, and the 0.25 kHz values are averages over those animals.

value: AN1 best frequency 4.5 to 5.1 kHz in nine of eleven animals, 4.4 kHz in two
eye: tympanal ear, read out from the AN1 ascending auditory interneuron; not an audiogram of the whole animal
method: neurophysiological tuning of one identified interneuron (AN1), threshold at one spike per syllable in three of five stimulations
conditions: Extracellular recording from the ascending interneuron AN1 with tungsten hook electrodes on the connectives between the prothoracic and suboesophageal ganglia; animals briefly anaesthetised with chlorethylene, fixed ventral side up, in a Faraday cage at 21 to 23 C. Teleogryllus oceanicus: 11 animals (3 males, 8 females) from a laboratory culture, used one week after the final moult. Stimulus was a pulsed pattern (23 ms pulses, 16 ms pauses, four pulses per chirp) with carrier 3.0 to 6 kHz; AN1 tuning was tested at 3.5 to 6 kHz for T. oceanicus (3.0 to 6 kHz for Teleogryllus commodus, so the frequency set differs between species and the lower edge cannot be compared across them). Threshold was the level giving at least one spike per syllable in at least three of five stimulations, in 1 dB steps; the maximum level is not stated.

source.authors: Kostarakos K, Hennig MR, Römer H
source.title: Two matched filters and the evolution of mating signals in four species of cricket

quote: Nine of eleven individuals in T.o. exhibited a tuning of AN1 between 4.5 to 5.1 kHz, but two individuals were tuned at 4.4 kHz, and were significantly less sensitive at higher frequencies.
note: Printed name T. oceanicus; accepted name Teleogryllus oceanicus (Le Guillou, 1841), valid on the Orthoptera Species File page (otus/829832; Gryllidae, Gryllinae). This is AN1 tuning, so it describes one neuron's best frequency, not the whole animal's hearing range, and nothing was tested below 3.5 kHz or above 6 kHz. Table 1 gives a mean-curve best frequency of 5.0 kHz (the Results text gives 4.85 kHz for the average tuning of all 11 animals; individual best frequencies 4.8 +/- 0.26 kHz, range 4.4 to 5.1) and a mean threshold of 39.9 dB SPL for this species; that row could not be quoted word for word, so only the range sentence is used. Males of the species call at a carrier near 4.8 kHz (Table 1). The paper's Methods and Results disagree for T. commodus (text 3.8 to 4 kHz, table range 3.4 to 4.5 kHz), which is why that species was not filed.
